title: Kids' Vaping Linked to Smoking, Health Issues
paragraphs: Vapes are often marketed as being safer than cigarettes. But a major review of the impacts of vaping on children and young people has found links with respiratory health problems, and a significantly increased likelihood of becoming cigarette smokers.
The review was done by the UK's Royal College of Paediatrics and Child Health (RCPCH), and included over 14,000 published articles and 400 studies.

Vaping hasn't been around for a very long time compared to other tobacco products. In the UK, e-cigarettes have only been available since 2007, which means there has been limited time to research their long-term health impacts.

According to the RCPCH review, vaping has become common among young people. A quarter of young people aged 11 to 16 in the UK say they've tried vaping, and 9% currently vape. These rates are more than double what they were in 2021.

The researchers found consistent links between vaping and poorer respiratory health. This included young people who vaped being more likely to report coughing, sneezing, bronchitis symptoms and worse asthma symptoms.
The impacts didn't end with respiratory health. The review also linked vaping with oral and dental health problems, as well as poor mental health outcomes, like anxiety and depression.

Importantly, the review also found strong evidence that young people who vaped were three times more likely to start smoking cigarettes — and cigarettes of course have their own well-known health risks, including respiratory diseases, cardiovascular disease and cancer.

Mike McKean from the RCPCH said, "Vaping is still a relatively new product, and there is much we do not yet know about its long-term impact on children and young people — but a clear and concerning picture is emerging."
He also called the UK's new Tobacco and Vapes Act an important step in protecting young people from nicotine addiction.

The new rules will limit how companies can describe the flavors of vapes and other nicotine products so they don't appeal to children. And from January 2027, the UK will start phasing out sales of tobacco products to anyone born after 2008.
